reproduction_target: Bioinformatic analysis of Agro-STARR-seq / ATAC-Agro-STARR-seq enhancer screens: (A) Arabidopsis Agro-STARR-seq read filtering, alignment, deduplication, MACS2 enhancer peak calling, enhancer annotation/conservation/epigenetic-state/motif/TE characterization; (B) DREAM deep-learning dataset construction, model training and genetic-algorithm enhancer design; (C) N. benthamiana ATAC-Agro-STARR-seq pipeline (Hansen et al. 2022 style) covering read processing, library-complexity and insert-size QC, Genrich accessibility peak calling, TSS/heatmap profiling with deepTools, public RNA-seq quantification (HISAT2/HTSeq/edgeR), active-region calling, TOBIAS footprinting, FIMO motif enrichment, clusterProfiler GO and StringTie transcript prediction. Wet-lab work (vector construction, library preparation, Agrobacterium infiltration, luciferase reporter assays, RT-PCR/qRT-PCR) is out of computational-reproduction scope.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis-invocation from the Methods sections 'Bioinformatic Analysis of Agro-STARR-seq in Arabidopsis', 'Deep learning model training and enhancer design (DREAM framework)' and 'Bioinformatic Pipeline and Analysis of ATAC-Agro-STARR-seq in N. benthamiana'. Reference-genome/annotation downloads (TAIR10, Niben261 from solgenomics, organelle sequences from CNCB, PlantTFDB v5.0, Ensembl Plants, PlantRegMap) are folded into the steps that consume them. The chi-square enrichment test is folded into the FIMO scanning step; blastn confirmation is folded into the StringTie step. No code repository, script archive, notebook or configuration is provided anywhere in the paper; the only named scripts (fastq_processing.py, call_ATAC-STARR_regulatory-regions.py) are cited by name from the published ATAC-STARR-seq pipeline (Hansen et al. 2022) without a URL, and the DREAM framework is cited to prior work with a filed patent and no repository. Wet-lab procedures counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: Fastp (v0.23.4) quality filtering of raw Arabidopsis Agro-STARR-seq input/output reads with '-w 5', other parameters default
Bowtie2 (v2.2.8) alignment to TAIR10 with '--wrapper basic-0 --very-sensitive -X 2000 --rg-id <index id>'
Duplicate removal per index library with Sambamba (no version, no command given)
MACS2 (v2.1.4) enhancer peak calling: 'callpeak -c <input bam> -t <output bam> --keep-dup all -q 0.05 --gsize 119667750 --nomodel'
Genome-wide enhancer distribution plot with R package 'ideogram' (no version, no parameters)
Enhancer genomic annotation with ChIPSeeker (v1.42.1) 'annotatePeak' using TxDb.Athaliana.BioMart.plantsmart51
PhastCons conservation analysis: scores from PlantRegMap, region annotations from Ensembl Plants, average score per enhancer and per genomic region (no tool/version/script stated)

Epigenetic-state analysis of public Arabidopsis epigenome data (GEO GSE183957 mature leaves, GSE233525 young shoots; H3K27ac/H3K9ac/H3K27me3/H3K4me1/H3K4me3/open chromatin): 'trimming, mapping, and filtering' with no tools, versions or parameters stated
Motif enrichment over 619 Arabidopsis TFs from PlantTFDB v5.0 using 'a custom script', background = shuffled non-enhancer regions
IGV visualization of ERF115 example locus based on published GEO GSE48793
Transposable-element overlap analysis using TAIR10 annotated TEs from TAIR (no tool/version/parameters stated)

DREAM training-dataset construction: random background regions equal in number to peaks with input DNA reads >30, +/-300 bp from peak midpoint, activity = log2FC of RNA RPKM over input DNA RPKM, reverse-complement augmentation, chr4 = validation / chr5 = test split

DREAM deep-learning model training (previously published framework, ref 24): learning rate 4e-5, batch size 256, 'other parameters remained consistent with our prior research'; no framework version, no repository, patent filed on DREAM
Genetic-algorithm synthetic enhancer design: 'initial population size, mutation rate, and other parameters were maintained as in our previous work' (ref 14); no code, no explicit values

N. benthamiana read processing of ATAC-seq / plasmid / Agrobacterium DNA and RNA libraries with 'fastq_processing.py' (script name from Hansen et al. 2022 ATAC-STARR-seq pipeline, no URL/version); reference Niben261 from solgenomics plus chloroplast C_AA066594.1 and mitochondrion C_AA066595.1 from CNCB; duplicates retained
Library-complexity estimation with Preseq (github.com/smithlabcode/preseq, version 3.2.0) 'lc_extrap' on duplicate-retained reads
Insert-size distribution with Picard (broadinstitute.github.io/picard, version 2.26.3) 'CollectInsertSizeMetrics'
ATAC-seq accessibility peak calling with Genrich (github.com/jsh58/Genrich, version 0.6.1); no command line given
Gene distribution of ATAC peaks / enhancers / histone peaks with ChIPSeeker (no version stated here), tssRegion = -2000/+1000 bp; Niben261 TxDb built with 'makeTxDbFromGFF' from GenomicFeatures
TSS enrichment profiles with deepTools (version 3.5.6) 'computeMatrix reference-point' + 'plotProfile'; gene locations/strands extracted from the GFF annotation
Trim Galore (github.com/FelixKrueger/TrimGalore, no version) filtering of three public N. benthamiana LAB leaf RNA-seq replicates SRR25703579/SRR25703580/SRR25703581
HISAT2 (version 2.2.1) alignment of the public RNA-seq to Niben261, retaining MAPQ >= 30
Gene-level counting with HTSeq-count (version 0.11.3); no mode/strandedness parameters given
FPKM normalization with the edgeR 'fpkm' function (no version), mean FPKM across three replicates

Active bin / active region identification with 'call_ATAC-STARR_regulatory-regions.py' (Hansen et al. 2022 script name, no URL/version) on duplicate-retained DNA and RNA libraries with ATAC-seq peaks as input peak set
Proximal/distal classification of active regions with ChIPSeeker 'annotatePeak' (promoter = -2000/+1000 bp of TSS)

Histone-modification heatmaps over proximal/distal regulatory regions with deepTools 'computeMatrix reference-point' + 'plotHeatmap' using public ChIP-seq SRR27031034 (H3K27ac), SRR27031032 (H3K4me3), SRR27031033 (H3K27me3), SRR27031030 (H3K9me2) and inputs SRR27031035, SRR27031031

TF footprinting within accessible peaks with TOBIAS (no version) applied to the DNA library, Arabidopsis motifs from PlantTFDB, bound/unbound defined by BINDetect; procedure 'similar to Hansen et al.'

Motif enrichment: FIMO scanning (no version) of Arabidopsis motifs in all/proximal/distal active regions vs 50,000 random background regions (mean length 115 bp, active regions excluded), followed by chi-square test
TCP ChIP-seq analysis of public datasets SRR15036661 and SRR15036676 (no tools, versions or parameters stated)
GO enrichment of genes annotated to TCP-bound active accessible peaks with clusterProfiler (no version); GO annotations from the eggNOG-mapper web service (no version, no run parameters)

Transcript prediction with StringTie (version v3.0.0) over Niben261Chr12:120,946,470-120,948,272 from RNA-seq reads, exon sequences confirmed against Araport11 CDS via blastn on the arabidopsis.org web server

headline.static_readiness: 0/32 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: Even under the most generous inference-inclusive reading, no computational step exceeds NI. The hard blocker is data: the Data availability statement reads in full 'Raw sequencing data will be made available upon publication', so the Agro-STARR-seq / ATAC-Agro-STARR-seq input, output, ATAC-seq and plasmid libraries that 24 of 32 steps consume are not deposited anywhere (no GEO/SRA/ENA/BioProject accession is given for data generated in this study). The eight steps that operate purely on public accessions (GSE183957, GSE233525, GSE48793, SRR25703579-81, SRR27031030-35, SRR15036661/76) cap at NI because no code repository, script, notebook or configuration exists anywhere in the paper. Exact version pins are given for a good subset of tools (fastp 0.23.4, Bowtie2 2.2.8, MACS2 2.1.4, ChIPSeeker 1.42.1, Preseq 3.2.0, Picard 2.26.3, Genrich 0.6.1, deepTools 3.5.6, HISAT2 2.2.1, HTSeq 0.11.3, StringTie 3.0.0) with no environment closure (no conda env, lockfile or container), and several tools are unversioned (Sambamba, ideogram, Trim Galore, edgeR, TOBIAS, FIMO, clusterProfiler, eggNOG-mapper, IGV). The DREAM deep-learning framework and its genetic algorithm are cited to prior work with a filed patent, no repository, no weights, and parameters given only by reference. There is no stage-2 code artifact to read; this paper cannot become R-star-eligible via stage-2 as published.
headline.coverage: 32 computational steps assessed from Methods prose (Arabidopsis Agro-STARR-seq analysis, DREAM model/design, N. benthamiana ATAC-Agro-STARR-seq pipeline); 8 wet-lab steps counted (W) but out of computational-reproduction scope. A Data availability statement is present but defers deposition ('upon publication'); no Code availability statement exists.

gaps.where: All data generated in this study (Arabidopsis Agro-STARR-seq input/output libraries, N. benthamiana ATAC-seq, plasmid, Agrobacterium DNA/RNA libraries) - blocks 24 of 32 C-steps
gaps.missing: Data availability states verbatim: 'Raw sequencing data will be made available upon publication.' No GEO/SRA/ENA/BioProject/figshare/Zenodo accession is provided for any newly generated dataset, and no processed intermediates (peak sets, enhancer BED files, active-region calls, DREAM training matrices, designed enhancer sequences) are deposited either.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the raw FASTQ libraries under a GEO/SRA (or ENA) accession and cite it in the paper, plus the derived enhancer/active-region BED files, the DREAM train/validation/test dataset splits, and the designed synthetic enhancer sequences.

gaps.missing: No code repository, script archive, notebook, workflow or configuration file is provided anywhere in the paper; there is no Code availability statement. The only named scripts (fastq_processing.py, call_ATAC-STARR_regulatory-regions.py) are referenced by filename from Hansen et al. 2022 without a URL or commit, and the motif enrichment step is 'a custom script' with no artifact.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit an analysis repository (GitHub + Zenodo DOI) containing the full command sequence, the custom motif-enrichment script, the exact fork/commit of the ATAC-STARR-seq scripts used, and the plotting code, plus a Code availability statement pointing at a versioned release.

gaps.where: Software environment for all named tools
gaps.missing: No conda environment, lockfile, requirements file or container image is mentioned. Version pins cover only a subset (fastp 0.23.4, Bowtie2 2.2.8, MACS2 2.1.4, ChIPSeeker 1.42.1, Preseq 3.2.0, Picard 2.26.3, Genrich 0.6.1, deepTools 3.5.6, HISAT2 2.2.1, HTSeq 0.11.3, StringTie 3.0.0); Sambamba, R package ideogram, Trim Galore, edgeR, TOBIAS, FIMO/MEME suite, clusterProfiler, GenomicFeatures, IGV and eggNOG-mapper are unversioned, and no R or Python version is stated anywhere.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a conda-lock / pixi.lock or a container digest covering both the shell-tool stack and the R/Bioconductor stack, and record R/Python versions and the deep-learning framework version used for DREAM.

gaps.where: DREAM deep-learning model (C13) and genetic-algorithm enhancer design (C14)
gaps.missing: No model architecture file, no trained weights, no framework/version, and no repository. Hyperparameters are given only as 'learning rate 4e-5, batch size 256, other parameters consistent with our prior research' and 'population size, mutation rate ... maintained as in our previous work'. A provisional patent (2023114102122) is filed on DREAM, which may further constrain artifact release. No random seed is stated for training, augmentation or the genetic algorithm.
gaps.how_to_close: Release the DREAM model code and trained checkpoint (or state the licensing constraint explicitly), enumerate all hyperparameters inline rather than by citation, and record seeds for the train/val/test split, augmentation and genetic-algorithm runs.

gaps.where: C3 (Sambamba), C7 (PhastCons averaging), C8 (public epigenome trimming/mapping/filtering), C11 (TE overlap), C18 (Genrich), C23 (HTSeq-count), C30 (TCP ChIP-seq)
gaps.missing: Several steps state only that an analysis 'was performed' with no tool, no command line and no thresholds: the public-epigenome processing ('Data processing, including trimming, mapping, and filtering, was performed'), the PhastCons averaging procedure, the TE overlap method, and the TCP ChIP-seq analysis. Genrich and HTSeq-count are named with versions but no parameters; Sambamba has neither.
gaps.how_to_close: State the tool, version and full command line for every processing step, including the reprocessing of the downloaded public datasets, the overlap/averaging definitions, and Genrich/HTSeq-count/Sambamba invocations.

gaps.where: C29 (FIMO background sampling), C12 (DREAM background region sampling), C9 (shuffled non-enhancer background)
gaps.missing: Three steps depend on random sampling or shuffling (50,000 random background regions; randomly selected background genomic regions equal in number to peaks; shuffled non-enhancer regions) with no random seed and no deposited background region set, so the enrichment statistics are not exactly reproducible.
gaps.how_to_close: Record and publish the random seeds, or deposit the generated background region sets as BED files alongside the enrichment code.

gaps.where: Reference genomes and annotation databases: TAIR10, Niben261 (solgenomics.net), organelle sequences C_AA066594.1 / C_AA066595.1 (CNCB), PlantTFDB v5.0, PlantRegMap PhastCons, Ensembl Plants, Araport11, eggNOG-mapper web service
gaps.missing: Only PlantTFDB carries a version (v5.0). Genome/annotation builds are named (TAIR10, Niben261, Araport11) but no release date, file name or checksum is given; Ensembl Plants and PlantRegMap downloads are undated; eggNOG-mapper was run through the web interface with no version or date, so its annotation snapshot is unrecoverable.
gaps.how_to_close: Pin every external resource by release/version and download date (ideally with checksums), and deposit the eggNOG-mapper output table rather than relying on the live web service.

gaps.missing: Wet-lab generation and validation steps are out of scope for computational reproduction (OOS); counted in W (8 steps), not verdicted.
